courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contribution: Mandatory first-year development.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.contribution: Complementary empirical tool: cleaning, manipulating and visualising tabular, spatial and text data, with a cross-disciplinary research project. Biomedical datasets and patient contact are not guaranteed.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contribution: Complementary quantitative tool: regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree methods, support-vector machines and clustering support predictive analysis. The course is general machine learning, not a biomedical bioinformatics sequence.

courses.name: Mathematical Methods
courses.contribution: provides mathematical foundations for the later probability and statistics course

courses.name: Probability & Statistics
courses.contribution: develops probability distributions, estimation and simulation for quantitative research

courses.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courses.contribution: Complementary conceptual foundation: knowledge, consciousness and philosophical argument prepare for the mind/emotion strand, rather than adding biomedical laboratory content.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contribution: Complementary normative method: moral theories, responsibility and reasoned judgments support appraisal of biomedical choices. The actual practical cases are general ethics, not a dedicated biomedical research-integrity or clinical-ethics course.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.contribution: Complementary conceptual inquiry: consciousness, personal identity, neurobiological explanations of mind and perceptual experience deepen the neuroscience route without substituting for experimental neuroscience.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.contribution: Complementary conceptual inquiry into emotions, rationality, well-being and moral judgment; this supports the neuroscience/mental-health question without claiming a clinical treatment course.

courses.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
courses.contribution: studies population patterns, disease risk and prevention through epidemiological evidence

courses.name: Functional Anatomy
courses.contribution: Direct human anatomy and function: body systems, surface anatomy, imaging, spatial reasoning and dissection-related academic encounters support biomedical mechanisms. These are academic learning experiences, not clinical-skills training.

courses.name: Pharmacology
courses.contribution: explains pharmacological action, therapeutic effects and toxicity of drugs

courses.name: Infection & Immunity
courses.contribution: studies pathogens, immune recognition and innate and adaptive defence

courses.name: Mechanisms of Disease
courses.contribution: compares normal physiology with disease mechanisms across cardiovascular, respiratory and other organ systems

courses.name: Neurobiology
courses.contribution: explores the neurobiology that underlies behaviour and physiological response

courses.name: Perception & Action
courses.contribution: studies sensory processing and neural control of action with cognitive-neuroscience methods

courses.name: Higher Order Functions
courses.contribution: develops advanced neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and cognitive-neuroscience experiment design

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.contribution: studies neural and psychological mechanisms of language processing

courses.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
courses.contribution: introduces cells, molecules and organ systems as foundations for biomedical explanation

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.contribution: introduces the biological and psychological study of brain and behaviour

courses.name: Molecular Cell Biology
courses.contribution: develops cellular mechanisms, including processes central to molecular disease biology

courses.name: Human Physiology
courses.contribution: examines regulation and functioning of adult human organ systems

courses.name: Biochemistry
courses.contribution: studies proteins, nucleic acids and metabolic reactions underlying cell function

courses.name: Life Science Laboratory
courses.contribution: provides hands-on biochemical and molecular laboratory techniques, including work with blood and microbes

courses.name: Molecular Pathology & Genetics
courses.contribution: examines human molecular pathology, genetics, inflammation and neoplasia

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.contribution: Direct quantitative method: multivariate statistical modelling, linear/logistic regression, factor analysis, ANOVA/ANCOVA and non-parametric testing support biomedical evidence analysis. The actual enriched content is statistical modelling; the title does not establish a separate experimental-design syllabus.

courses.name: Abnormal Psychology
courses.contribution: examines mental disorders across the lifespan through biological, psychological and social explanations

courses.name: Medical & Health Psychology
courses.contribution: examines biological, psychological and social determinants of illness and health interventions

courses.name: Advanced Research Seminar
courses.contribution: Direct evidence-synthesis method: systematic review and meta-analysis using R estimate effects and compare evidence across studies. It does not supply a new primary biomedical experiment or the extended research internship.

courses.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courses.contribution: studies psychological development across the lifespan, including interactions among developmental influences

HCBLIFE214: Partial laboratory-method correspondence: biochemical and molecular laboratory work, including proteins, blood, microbes and DNA, relates to the first-semester enzyme and genetic-laboratory assignments. Radboud also includes etiological research and other integrated work.
DISDATA111: Partial data-method correspondence: the current Radboud research unit explicitly includes an introduction to data science and analysis of students’ own data. UCR supplies general data handling and visualisation, rather than the full biomedical practical line.
HCBBIOM111: Partial epidemiological correspondence: Radboud includes a cancer-epidemiology assignment and critical appraisal alongside signal-transduction and muscle-activity tasks. UCR develops disease-pattern, risk and population-evidence reasoning; it does not reproduce the full integrated research unit.
HCBPSYC211: Partial quantitative-method correspondence: Radboud’s unit includes statistics and bioinformatics/big-data assignments; UCR develops applied multivariate models and statistical analysis. It does not reproduce the government-advice or biomedical-data sequence.
